simple.meaning: כָּכָה (kâkâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “just so , referring to the previous or following context.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 12:11. The surrounding context includes family, family line.

definitions.short: just so , referring to the previous or following context
definitions.usage: after that (this) manner, this matter, (even) so, in such a case, thus.
definitions.full: H3602. kakah כָּ֫כָה 37 adverb thus (Late Hebrew abbreviated to כָּךְ , with prepositions כָּךְ בֵּין meanwhile , לְפִיכָךְ therefore ; probably either from כָה and כְּ , literally as thus , Ol § 223 h ; or from כָה כָּה Kö ii. 1, 253 ), somewhat more emphatic than כֹּה , usually prefixed to word which it qualifies: — Exod 12:11 אתו תאכלו וככה and thus shall ye eat it, 29:35 ; Num 8:26 ; 11:15 לי עשׂה את ככה ואם , 15:11-12 , 13 ; Deut 25:9 ; 29:23 (compare 1Kin 9:8 ; Jer 22:8 ); so often with עשׂה : 1Sam 19:17 רמיתני ככה למה why hast thou thus deceived me ? 2Sam 17:21 ; 1Kin 1:6 , 48 ; Jer 13:9 ; 19:11 ; 28:11 ; 51:64 ; once with an adjective 2Sam 13:4 דל כָכָה אתה מדוע why art thou thus lean ? Eccl 11:5 answering to כַּאֲשֶׁר ; Psa 144:15 לוֺ שֶׁכָּכָה העם the people to which it is thus. Once 2Chr 18:19 repeated, in this way . . . in that way (|| 1Kin 22:20 בְּכֹהבְּ֗֗֗כֹה ). compare the synonym כָּזֹאת . With a preposition once, in late Hebrew, Est 9:26 עַלכָּֿ֫כָה concerning such a matter. With the interrogative אֵיכָכָה אי, how ? (p. 32).
